title: Portfolio 7: Next Steps
text:
My thesis project was a loose replication of a project that look at self-other agreement in a Sri Lankan sample of trauma surviviors. One big difference was the scale used, and the posttraumatic growth inventory (PTGI) used in the previous study is multidimensional. What this allows is a deeper dive into the level of agreement by being able to unpack ‘normative’ and ‘distinctive’ elements of agreement at the domain-level. This allows a much more confident interpretation of any observed agreement, by being able to say that pairs don’t all agree in broad normative way, and that the agreement is distinctive and unique to each pair. Fortunately, the previous study uploaded all their data and R-Script to an online repository. So, the purpose of this study is to try and replicate their analysis, which will be something I want to do it in future projects - perhaps even one this semester I am looking at with relationship satisfaction among couples. Profile.cjr <- function(x.set, y.set, nomiss = 0.8, distinct = TRUE, trim = TRUE) {
  valids <- apply(cbind(x.set, y.set), 1, function(z) {
    valid.pairs(z[1:ncol(x.set)], z[-(1:ncol(x.set))])$Pct
  })

  mat <- suppressWarnings(cor(t(x.set), t(y.set), use = "pair"))
  if (trim) {
    mat[mat == 1]  <- 0.9999999
    mat[mat == -1] <- -0.9999999
  }
  overall.r <- diag(mat)
  overall.r[valids < nomiss] <- NA

  baseline <- mean(psych::fisherz(mat[upper.tri(mat)]), na.rm = TRUE)

  x.Norm <- colMeans(x.set, na.rm = TRUE)
  y.Norm <- colMeans(y.set, na.rm = TRUE)
  x.dist <- multicon::temp.resid(x.Norm, x.set, nomiss = nomiss)
  y.dist <- multicon::temp.resid(y.Norm, y.set, nomiss = nomiss)
  mat2 <- suppressWarnings(cor(t(x.dist), t(y.dist), use = "pair"))
  if (trim) {
    mat2[mat2 == 1]  <- 0.9999999
    mat2[mat2 == -1] <- -0.9999999
  }
  dist.r <- diag(mat2)
  dist.r[valids < nomiss] <- NA

  overall.test <- t.test(psych::fisherz(overall.r), mu = baseline)
  dist.test    <- t.test(psych::fisherz(dist.r),    mu = 0)

  tests <- data.frame(
    Agreement = c(
      N        = sum(!is.na(overall.r)),
      Mean     = psych::fisherz2r(mean(psych::fisherz(overall.r), na.rm = TRUE)),
      Baseline = psych::fisherz2r(baseline),
      t        = overall.test$statistic,
      p.value  = overall.test$p.value
    ),
    Distinctive = c(
      N        = sum(!is.na(dist.r)),
      Mean     = psych::fisherz2r(mean(psych::fisherz(dist.r), na.rm = TRUE)),
      Baseline = 0,
      t        = dist.test$statistic,
      p.value  = dist.test$p.value
    )
  )

  list(
    Agreement = data.frame(Overall = overall.r, Distinctive = dist.r),
    Tests     = round(tests, 3)
  )
}

For this portfolio piece, I have taken the opportunity to complete a task for my RAship, in which he asked me to create a visually appealing / informative way to describe the demographics of a study he is presenting on at the WISE conference.I decided to give him the option of two separate charts, or the faceted combined figure at the end. # Splitting gender and sexual orientation
data$Gender_Identity <- data$Please.select.your.gender.identity.ies...select.all.that.apply.....Selected.Choice
data$Sexual_Orientation <- data$Please.indicate.if.you.identify.as.any.of.the.following..you.can.select.multiple....Selected.Choice

# Create simplified ethnic labels
data <- data %>%
  mutate(Ethnicity = case_when(
    grepl("White/ European", Please.select.your.ethnic.identity.ies..) ~ "White",
    grepl("Black/ African", Please.select.your.ethnic.identity.ies..) ~ "Black",
    grepl("Asian", Please.select.your.ethnic.identity.ies..) ~ "Asian",
    grepl("Latin", Please.select.your.ethnic.identity.ies..) ~ "Latino",
    grepl("American Indian", Please.select.your.ethnic.identity.ies..) ~ "Indigenous",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ))


# Preparing data for sexual orientation chart
orientation_data <- data %>%
  separate_rows(Sexual_Orientation, sep = ",") %>%
  group_by(Sexual_Orientation, Ethnicity) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(n >= 3)  # Filtering for visual clarity

# Creating the bar chart for sexual orientation
ggplot(orientation_data, aes(x = Sexual_Orientation, y = n, fill = Ethnicity)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Sexual Orientation by Ethnic Group",
       x = "Sexual Orientation", y = "") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))









# Preparing data for gender identity chart
gender_data <- data %>%
  separate_rows(Gender_Identity, sep = ",") %>%
  group_by(Gender_Identity, Ethnicity) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(n >= 2)  # Filtering for visual clarity

  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Gender Identity by Ethnic Group",
       x = "Gender Identity", y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

combined_data <- data %>%
  gather(key = "Type", value = "Identity", Gender_Identity, Sexual_Orientation) %>%
  separate_rows(Identity, sep = ",") %>%
  count(Type, Identity, Ethnicity) %>%
  filter(n >= 2) # again, for clarity

# Creating faceted charts
ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = Identity, y = n, fill = Ethnicity)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  facet_wrap(~ Type, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Gender Identity and Sexual Orientation by Ethnic Group",
       x = "", y = "") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel") +

title: Portfolio 6: Exploratory Analyses
text:
The purpose of these analyses was to explore whether any of the additional variables measured (such as depression, intimacy, confidence) would moderate the relationship between self- and partner-reports of posttratumatic growth. For example, we thought that higher ‘thoughtfulness’ in response may lead to higher corroboration, i.e. a higher trait-level agreement.I hate to spoil it for you, but all moderators were null, thus why the main analysis part got sheered down a little.
